name: Changing a vehicle into your name after buying it
summary: Transferring a used vehicle from the seller's name into yours at DVLA. A different transaction from registering a vehicle for the first time.
aliases: I bought a pre-owned car from someone, how can I change the ownership to my name
change of ownership of a vehicle
how do I put the car in my name
I bought a used car, what do I do
the car is still in the seller's name
I buy car from someone, how I go change the name

eligibility.text: Transfer of vehicle ownership is one of the services DVLA offers, separate from first registration and from renewal of registration.
This is the route when the vehicle is already on the register in somebody else's name. Registering a vehicle for the first time is a different transaction with a different document set.
Until the transfer is done the vehicle remains recorded against the seller. That matters for anything the register is used to decide - which is the reason to do it promptly rather than eventually.
DVLA inspects and tests motor vehicles as a statutory function, so expect the vehicle to be seen rather than only its paperwork.

documents.name: The vehicle's existing registration documents, from the seller
documents.where_to_obtain: The person selling you the vehicle
documents.note: Get these before money changes hands. A seller who cannot produce them is the single most common way this goes wrong.

documents.name: Proof of the sale - a receipt or bill of sale signed by both of you
The seller's identification
documents.note: Both parties are normally required to be identifiable to the transaction.

steps.action: Before paying, confirm the vehicle is registered in the seller's own name and that they hold the registration documents
Agree the sale in writing, signed by both parties
Apply for transfer of ownership at a DVLA office, with the seller's cooperation
Present the vehicle if DVLA requires inspection, and pay the transfer fee
Collect the registration documents showing you as the owner

fees.label: Transfer of ownership
fees.note: DVLA's 2026 price list covers transfers, but publishes the figures only inside a slide deck rather than as text we could read. Ask at the office before you go.

timeline.note: DVLA publishes no turnaround time for a transfer.

rejection_causes.text: The seller cannot produce the registration documents, or the vehicle turns out not to be registered in their name.
The seller becomes unreachable after payment. A transfer generally needs their cooperation, which is why the paperwork belongs before the money.
Treating this as a fresh registration. It is a transfer of an existing record, and asking for the wrong transaction wastes the trip.

caveats.text: DVLA names transfer of ownership as a service but publishes no document checklist, no fee and no timeline for it. Everything here beyond 'DVLA does this, and it is not the same as first registration' is our reading rather than DVLA's published word - which is why this card is marked Tier 2. Ring the office and confirm before you travel.
Insurance is a separate matter with a private insurer, not with DVLA. Transferring the registration does not transfer or renew cover.

name: Registering a product with the FDA before you sell it
summary: The approval a regulated product needs from the Food and Drugs Authority before it goes on the market, and how long each category takes.
aliases: I want FDA to approve my product before sending it to the market
how do I register my product with FDA
I want to sell my food product
I make soap, do I need approval
how do I get my product certified before selling
product must be approved before market

clarifiers.question: What kind of product is it?

options.label: Cosmetic, household chemical or medical device

eligibility.text: The FDA registers products in six groups: food; drugs and nutraceuticals; herbal and homeopathic medicines; vaccines and biological products; medical devices, cosmetics and household chemicals; and tobacco and substances of abuse.
The FDA operates under the Public Health Act, 2012 (Act 851).

If your product is not in one of those groups, the FDA is probably not the right body. Conformity to a published standard is the Ghana Standards Authority's Standard Mark, which is a different question from safety.
The FDA processes new applications, renewals and variations, so an approval is not permanent - a change to the product or its label may need a variation.
Applications for food and feed intended for animal consumption go through the same food route.
Cosmetics, household chemicals and medical devices are handled together as one registration stream.

documents.name: A G-FIRMS account
documents.note: The FDA's e-services portal, used for product registration and facility licensing submissions.

documents.name: The application form for your product category
documents.note: Food has separate forms for imported and locally made products.

documents.name: Your business registration
documents.where_to_obtain: Office of the Registrar of Companies

documents.name: Product samples for analysis
documents.note: The FDA excludes applications requiring laboratory confirmation from its faster premium timelines, so samples and testing apply to some products and not others. Confirm for yours.

documents.name: Your product label and packaging artwork
documents.note: The FDA lists label evaluation as a service it charges for, so labels are assessed rather than assumed.

steps.action: Create an account on the G-FIRMS portal
Complete the application form for your product category and submit it with the supporting documents
Supply samples and allow site verification where your product needs them
steps.location: Your premises or an FDA laboratory
steps.note: These are the applications the FDA excludes from its premium timelines.

steps.action: Wait for the assessment and respond to any queries raised
Receive the registration and check it appears on the FDA's public product register

fees.label: Registration fee
fees.note: The FDA does not publish a fee schedule on the product registration pages. Fees vary by product category and by whether the product is imported or locally made. Ask the FDA, or check the fee schedule in the guideline document for your category.

fees.label: Premium service
fees.note: The FDA's own wording. It buys a shorter timeline, not a different outcome.

timeline.standard: 30 working days for a regular application
timeline.expedited: Premium service: 15 working days for a new low-risk application, 10 for a renewal, 5 for a request
timeline.note: Premium timelines exclude anything needing laboratory confirmation, site verification, supermarket products, or a due diligence request - so a product that needs testing does not get the fast route at any price.

rejection_causes.text: Putting the product on the market before the registration is granted.
Assuming premium service will speed up a product that needs laboratory confirmation. The FDA excludes those from premium timelines.
A label that does not survive evaluation, so the file goes back and forth.
Changing the formulation or the label after approval without applying for a variation.

caveats.text: The FDA publishes its categories and its timelines clearly, but not its fees or a single document checklist - those live in per-category guideline PDFs. Treat the document list here as the shape of what is wanted, and get the definitive list from the guideline for your category.

Whether your particular product is regulated, and under which category, is a determination for the FDA. We can tell you what the categories are and how the process runs; we cannot classify your product for you.

name: Getting the Ghana Standards Authority Standard Mark for your product
summary: Third-party certification that a product conforms to a published standard, and the Standard Mark that goes on the packaging.
aliases: how do I get the standard mark
I want my product certified to a standard

eligibility.text: GSA product certification is 'assessment and impartial third-party attestation that fulfilment of specified requirement has been demonstrated' - that a product conforms to a defined standard for performance, safety, interoperability or sustainability.
A certified product carries the Standard Mark on its packaging and certificate, with a reference number or the name of the product standard, as a third-party guarantee of compliance.

This answers a different question from FDA registration. The FDA decides whether a regulated product may be sold at all; GSA attests that a product meets a published standard. A food or cosmetic product may need the FDA regardless of whether it seeks the Standard Mark.
GSA also inspects imports, which is a separate function from certifying a producer's own product.

documents.name: Application for Licence to Use the Standard Mark
The supporting documents named in GSA's applicant guidelines
documents.where_to_obtain: GSA's General Guidelines for Applicants of Product Certification
documents.note: Published as a PDF rather than as a web page, which is why we cannot list the contents here.

steps.action: Read GSA's General Guidelines for Applicants of Product Certification and identify the standard your product would be certified against
Submit the Application for Licence to Use the Standard Mark with its supporting documents
Allow assessment of the product and of how its production is supervised and controlled
steps.note: GSA's description of certification includes that 'production has been supervised and controlled', so the process looks at how you make it, not only at the finished item.

fees.label: Certification
fees.note: GSA publishes no fee for product certification on its website. Ask GSA directly.

timeline.note: GSA publishes no timeline for product certification.

rejection_causes.text: Applying to GSA for something the FDA regulates, or the reverse. They answer different questions.
Treating certification as a test of one sample. GSA's own wording covers how production is supervised and controlled.

caveats.text: This is a Tier 2 card and deliberately short. GSA describes what certification means and names the application form, but publishes no step list, no fee, no timeline and no validity period on its website - the detail sits inside guideline PDFs. Get the specifics from GSA before planning around them.
Whether the Standard Mark is required for your product, or is a commercial choice that helps you sell, depends on the product and the market you are selling into. That is a question for GSA.
